h1: Painters in Archer, FL for Farmhouses, Ranches, and Main-Street Buildings
heroIntro: Precision Paint Experts is a Newberry-based painting contractor that works across rural west Alachua County. In Archer that means open-country farmhouses, ranch homes, and a handful of older downtown commercial buildings.

sections.h2: A painting contractor next door to Archer
body: Our home base is Newberry, so Archer is a short drive down the road rather than a far corner of the service area. Archer property owners hire a local company that is licensed, bonded, and fully insured as a painting contractor in Archer, FL, brings 15+ years at the trade, and puts its own employees on every ladder. Once you sign, the job stays with us; it is never passed to a sub.

Out here west of Gainesville, Archer still looks like the country town it is: farmhouses well back from the road, ranch houses on a few acres each, and a short row of old commercial buildings downtown. That mix calls for a painter equally comfortable on a tall farmhouse gable and a masonry storefront.

sections.h2: What we see on Archer homes and buildings
body: Most of our Archer calls come from three directions. In Downtown Archer, the older commercial buildings carry masonry, stucco, and wood trim that have been painted many times, so the work starts with finding out which layers are still bonded. In Holly Hills and Archer Estates, we tend to see ranch homes with long rooflines, deep eaves, and fascia that takes the brunt of gutter overflow. On the farm and ranch properties in between, it is lap siding, porches, outbuildings, and board fencing.

Each of those wants a different system. On farmhouse clapboard and ranch trim we brush and spray an all-acrylic finish. Block, brick, and stucco that is moving at fine cracks get elastomeric. Where you want weathered boards to keep reading as wood, a stain that soaks into the grain replaces paint that would sit on top as a film.

sections.h2: Open fields, full sun, and damp porches around Archer
body: A house in a subdivision is shaded by its neighbors. A farmhouse in an open field is not. Archer homes often take full sun on every elevation, so the south and west walls chalk and fade years before the north side does, and sandy soil splashes up the bottom courses every time it pours.

The flip side is moisture. Any face that stays damp, such as a porch ceiling, a shaded north wall, or the boards closest to irrigation, grows mildew and algae quickly in this climate. During prep on Archer houses, mildew is killed rather than just rinsed, questionable boards are checked with a moisture meter, and rotten fascia or trim comes off and gets replaced instead of painted. Our article on hidden moisture behind siding shows the signs to look for.

sections.h2: An Archer job, start to finish
body: Reach out and an Archer walkthrough is generally booked within 48 hours. It is done by a crew lead, not a commission salesperson, who tapes off measurements, photographs the house and outbuildings, and checks suspect wood with a moisture meter. Within about one business day you receive the written, itemized estimate, with in-scope and out-of-scope surfaces, each prep step, the primer and finish by name, the coat count, and the timeline. If anything is added later, it happens only with your written okay.

Crews typically arrive one to three weeks after approval. Opening days go to preparation: a wash, mildew treatment, scraping and sanding, popped nails reset, rotten fascia and trim repaired, new caulk, and primer on bare spots. The finish is two full coats, or three when the color swing is large or the wood is dry and thirsty. On an Archer farmhouse, the painting itself usually takes three to seven working days, and washing and drying add time to that; the friendliest exterior months run from October to May.
You sign the final punch walk only after every item is corrected. Labelled leftover paint stays in your barn or garage, and the exterior workmanship is covered in writing for up to 10 years.

Our crews move between Archer and the surrounding communities every week. To the north is our home town of Newberry, and to the east is Gainesville. Heading west into Levy County we work in Williston, and southeast of Archer we paint the older homes of Micanopy. Every county and town we cover appears on the service area page.

faqs.q: Do you paint rural properties outside Archer's town limits?
faqs.a: Yes. Acreage outside town, with its farmhouses, ranch houses, barns, and fence lines, makes up a steady share of our Archer work. During the walkthrough the crew lead writes down access, distances, and every outbuilding so none of it is left off the estimate.

faqs.q: How quickly can you come out to Archer for an estimate?
faqs.a: Usually within 48 hours, and your itemized quote follows about one business day after that. Once approved, an Archer job generally starts one to three weeks out.

faqs.q: Are your Archer crews licensed and insured?
faqs.a: Yes. We are licensed and bonded in Florida with full insurance, and workers' comp covers each painter on our crews. A commercial owner or HOA can have an insurance certificate issued in its own name ahead of mobilization.

faqs.q: What paint do you use on Archer farmhouses?
faqs.a: We pull from premium Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore lines. Farmhouse siding and trim take an all-acrylic paint, any stucco with fine cracks takes elastomeric, and porch boards or rails you want to keep natural take a penetrating stain. Your estimate names the specific product.
